title: The Auth: one lockout point for remote access
summary: Design decided by Tom Dyer, 24 Nov 2026 (not built). A shell gets an Auth: not a logon. A logon may request one, but getting an Auth is a request-and-lock operation: the Auth is locked to the shell that requested it (session, process, principal). The Auth key lives in a su-locked account (no login shell, locked password, reached only by su from root), validated through one means only; that account signs for the shell, like ssh-agent: the shell holds a handle, never the key, so an LLM in the shell cannot copy it. RTO2 requests are signed under the Auth for n, where n is both a number of requests and a time window, whichever runs out first. On the target host the request runs under the Auth's delegate (a local principal with its own NewShell policy); if the Auth has no delegate on that host, RTO2 rejects it. Locking the Auth stops remote access everywhere: because every signature passes the su-locked account, receivers accept a grant until n runs out and do not call the authority per request (Tom: signing there is sufficient).
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: An Auth is requested and locked, never implied by a logon
The Auth key never leaves the su-locked account; it signs, the shell asks
n is both a count and a time window
No delegate on the host: RTO2 rejects
One lockout point: lock the Auth
procedure: Build on the dev4 verifier slot: an AlchemyRTOAuthVerifier asking the host validator
Add RTO_AUTH_LOCKED, RTO_AUTH_EXPIRED and RTO_NO_DELEGATE to admit
Put the delegate decision in the RTO2 identity seam (IdentityDirectory~aclDecision, rexxos_rto2_grid dev16/dev17)
Claude's additions, not yet ruled on: a request counter per Auth so a signed request cannot be replayed within n; a second check at activation so an Auth locked after delivery still stops the run
Reuse the SSC pattern (signed challenge, short-lived session, revocation per request, fresh challenge for sensitive actions) rather than a second scheme
